circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi that has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. Designed by Hermann Tilke, the circuit became the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside supporting motorsport categories. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 classification, qualifying it to stage world championship racing events.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following a rebuild and redesign that shortened the track, it was rebranded and once again hosted the Grand Prix during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street course in Azerbaijan's capital city that stretches 6. 003 km, ranking it among the longest venues on the Formula One schedule. The circuit hosted its first F1 race as the 2016 European Grand Prix, before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 kilometers and hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix in the Middle East that year. Beyond F1, the facility accommodates various motorsport categories including GP2 racing, drag racing, and 24-hour endurance events, while Australian V8 Supercars competed there from 2006 to 2010 in the Desert 400 series.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657-kilometre motorsport venue combines extended straightaways with diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for racing machinery. The track accommodates over 140,000 spectators and holds the highest FIA safety certification grade.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located in the Walloon region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has been a fixture of Formula One racing since the sport's inaugural 1950 season. The venue has continuously hosted the Belgian Grand Prix annually since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, this 4. 361 km circuit serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond its primary role in elite motorsport, the venue has welcomed various international racing series including sports car championships and North American open-wheel competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit, located in Shanghai's Jiading District, hosted the Chinese Grand Prix from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The venue has expanded its motorsport calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix beginning in 2024 alongside the Formula One event.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Northamptonshire in England, Silverstone Circuit hosted the inaugural 1948 British Grand Prix and later the inaugural 1950 Formula One World Championship race. After alternating with two other venues throughout the mid-twentieth century, the British Grand Prix has been a permanent fixture at Silverstone since 1987.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest hosted Formula One's debut race behind the Iron Curtain in 1986, becoming a permanent venue for the Hungarian Grand Prix on its 4. 381 km layout. Built in record time at just eight months after construction began in late 1985, the circuit was established outside the city near a highway rather than as a street course through Budapest's main park, fulfilling the sport's desire for Eastern European representation following recommendations to pursue Hungary over the Soviet Union.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Monza in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km speedway constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest permanent racing facility and the world's third such circuit. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, the track earned the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its distinctive long straights and fast corners that characterize its high-speed layout.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, spans 5. 807 kilometers and serves as a premier venue for Formula One racing alongside Japanese Super Formula competition. Operated by Honda Mobilityland, the track accommodates 155,000 spectators and has established itself as one of motorsport's most significant racing facilities.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that winds through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating iconic venues along Las Vegas Boulevard such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas. The track navigates through the famous hospitality district that defines the city's entertainment landscape.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both of whom died in racing accidents during the 1960s and early 1970s. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix across three distinct eras, with the current continuous run beginning in 2015 on its present layout.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary street circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners that allows qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by specialist circuit designers, the track was created specifically to host the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar starting in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, circling Monaco's harbour. Though officially named after the principality, it is widely known as the Monte Carlo circuit due to its location within the Monte Carlo area.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that rejoined the Formula One calendar in 2021 to host the revived Dutch Grand Prix. The venue's partnership with Formula One will conclude following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit sits north of Doha in Qatar and spans 5. 419 kilometres with a principal straight measuring 1. 068 kilometres.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise racing circuit that opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal plane crash in 1977. The venue hosts major motorsport events and features an adjacent kart track dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along the Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, which has served as the home of the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural appearance in 2021. The track also began hosting the Formula E racing series in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's waterfront district, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang neighborhoods into its layout as a temporary street-based racing venue.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya is a 4. 657 km Spanish motorsport venue located in Montmeló near Barcelona, featuring a diverse mix of extended straightaways and corner configurations that make it representative of modern circuit design. Boasting FIA Grade 1 credentials and spectator seating for approximately 140,700 people, the track serves as a comprehensive test of driver and vehicle performance.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas spans 3. 426 miles and holds the highest FIA grade classification for racing facilities. The track currently hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside NASCAR, MotoGP, and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance event, while previously accommodating various other international and domestic racing series.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon, a dual Thai and British nationality driver, represents Thailand on the Formula One grid while racing for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Fernando Alonso is a Spanish driver currently racing for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 alongside 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, he has achieved remarkable success in endurance motorsport, winning the World Endurance Championship, twice triumphing at Le Mans, and claiming victory at Daytona, making him uniquely the sole driver to have won both Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli competes for Mercedes in Formula One, having claimed six Grand Prix victories since entering the championship in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team. He has established himself as a competitor in the sport's premier motorseries.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabriel Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One, representing the Audi team in his racing career.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas has secured two runner-up finishes in the championship standings while driving for Mercedes in 2019 and 2020, accumulating 10 race victories throughout his 13-year Formula One career. He currently competes for Cadillac in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine driver Franco Alejandro Colapinto currently races in Formula One as part of the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan combines his role as a reserve driver for Haas in Formula One with racing in the European Le Mans Series' LMP2 category for Nielsen Racing. He made seven Grand Prix appearances across the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver previously achieved victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian motorsport competitor who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, representing France.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton, a British motorsport competitor, currently races for Ferrari in Formula One. The seven-time world champion holds multiple all-time records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes, equaling Michael Schumacher's championship tally.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi, while also boasting significant success in endurance motorsport, including a Le Mans 24 Hours victory achieved with Porsche in 2015.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand motorsport competitor, currently races for Racing Bulls in the Formula One championship.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver competing for Ferrari, finished second in the 2022 world championship standings and has secured nine race victories throughout his Formula One career spanning nine seasons.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, a Danish driver known as K-Mag, returned to Formula One competition between 2022 and 2024 after an earlier stint from 2014 to 2020. Currently, he competes primarily in the World Endurance Championship as a BMW factory driver for WRT, while also taking part-time racing in NASCAR's top series.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver for McLaren who claimed the 2025 World Drivers' Championship with the team. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has secured 12 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. Earlier in his career, he achieved a Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio "Checo" Pérez is a Mexican driver currently racing in Formula One for Cadillac. The experienced competitor finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has accumulated six Grand Prix victories over his 15-season career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri has claimed nine Formula One victories over his four-season career with McLaren, where he currently races.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One throughout a 14-season career spanning 2011 to 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his time in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Mercedes who has claimed seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish racing driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-year career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant competed in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery for Era Motorsport in IMSA competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently competing in Formula One with the Aston Martin team.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver who has held reserve positions with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls during his Formula One involvement spanning 2021 to 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver races for Red Bull Racing under the Dutch flag and has secured four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12-season Formula One career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, the sole Chinese driver to have competed in Formula One, raced in the championship from 2022 to 2024 before moving into a reserve role. He currently holds a reserve driver position with Cadillac in the series.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Alpine Racing competes from its Enstone base as Renault's works team after being rebranded from Renault F1 Team in 2021 to represent the French carmaker's Alpine sports car division, though Renault exited Formula One at the end of 2025. The team's only victory in its Alpine guise came through Esteban Ocon's triumph at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, and it currently operates with Mercedes power units.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has maintained a presence in Formula One across multiple organizational structures, with its current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited and competing under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, competing continuously since the championship's inception in 1950. The squad, famously nicknamed after their emblematic horse symbol, has maintained an unbroken presence throughout the sport's entire history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One team founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas, the organization entered F1 competition in 2016. Led by team principal Ayao Komatsu following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, the squad has competed continuously since its inaugural season.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss engineering firm, established in 1970 by Peter Sauber, initially built sports cars before transitioning to Formula One machinery as an independent manufacturer. The outfit achieved notable success in endurance racing, including a Le Mans victory in 1989, before competing in Formula One from 1993 until its acquisition by Audi in 2024, ultimately concluding its F1 operations in 2025 as one of the sport's longest-tenured constructors.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its dedicated facility in Woking, operating as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under the ownership of Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 through team ownership and engine supply arrangements. The current incarnation, Mercedes-AMG Petronas, operates from Brackley under a German licence and became a three-way partnership in January 2022 when Ineos joined Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff as equal stakeholders. The marque's racing efforts are traditionally associated with the "Silver Arrows" designation.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024, operating as part of Red Bull's two-team structure alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull GmbH's second official racing outfit in the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024, operating as the second team under Red Bull GmbH's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with a Milton Keynes facility near its sister team, the outfit represents Red Bull's expanded presence on the grid.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, based in England under an Austrian license, has been a dominant force in Formula One since its 2005 formation as part of the Red Bull GmbH conglomerate. Christian Horner led the team through two decades of success before Laurent Mekies assumed management in 2025, while the company also operates the separate Racing Bulls team.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, is a British Formula One constructor based in Grove, Oxfordshire. The team emerged following the failure of Williams's previous racing operation and will compete in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team name.
